title: API contract negotiator, compatibility safety-net, and migration harness for streaming/tool-calls/structured outputs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: We are introducing a negotiated API version header and several behavior flags that affect streaming token framing, tool/function call wire format, and structured output schemas. Without a robust compatibility strategy we risk regressions for customers who rely on older streaming delimiters, legacy tool-call payloads, or previous structured-output keys. Goal: Implement a runtime-side 'contract negotiator' that performs header-based version negotiation, exposes a backward-compatibility adapter layer for serving, and provides an automated migration harness that runs shadow regression tests across streaming, tool-calls, and structured outputs before any deprecation rollout. This ticket coordinates building the core runtime negotiation, the adapter shims, and the CI-driven migration tests, plus a developer-facing migration guide and CLI checks for customers to validate their integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts X-Redwood-API-Version header and falls back deterministically when absent
Behavior flags expose a matrix mapping (old behavior -> new behavior) and are honored by adapter layer
Compatibility adapter can translate streaming delimiters and token-frame boundaries bidirectionally for at least two legacy client patterns
Tool/function call wire-format adapter supports v1 and v2 payload shapes; automatic fallback exercised in test harness
Structured output schemas are versioned and conversion scripts exist for main public shapes (response.items, response.metadata, response.tools)
CI migration harness runs golden-prompt regression tests and produces a human-readable compatibility report with token-level diffs
Migration guide drafted and published with examples for Node/Python SDKs and a compatibility-check CLI command
No customer-facing incidents during a staged canary rollout across 3 regions when toggling the new behavior flags
tasks: Design header negotiation protocol and compatibility rules (runtime + SDK expectations)
Implement version negotiation in gateway and annotate request traces
Build adapter layer for streaming frame translations and integrate into serving runtime
Add tool-call adapter that maps legacy fields to v2 and vice versa
Create structured-output conversion scripts and forward-compatible schema registry entries
Construct CI migration harness: golden prompt corpus, per-model baselines, token-level diff tooling
Author migration guide and quick-check CLI for customers
Run internal shadow rollout and record regression metrics; iterate on adapters
Coordinate with Docs, SDK, and PM for public deprecation timeline and behavior flag rollout plan

notes: Key engineering trade-offs: (1) perform translation at gateway vs in each runtime instance (gateway centralizes logic but increases latency risk), (2) support per-tenant pinned versions vs global rollout (per-tenant increases complexity for adapters and caches). Proposed path: gateway negotiation + lightweight runtime adapters with a TTL’ed conversion cache to keep latency within SLOs. We will measure p50/p95 latency impact under shadow traffic before enabling adapters in production.
